original_record.question: Determine the number of non-degenerate rectangles whose edges lie completely on the grid lines of the following figure.\n<image1>
original_record.solution: First, let us count the total number of rectangles in the grid without the hole in the middle. There are $\left(\begin{array}{l}7 \ 2\end{array}\right)=21$ ways to choose the two vertical boundaries of the rectangle, and there are 21 ways to choose the two horizontal boundaries of the rectangles. This makes $21^2=441$ rectangles. However, we must exclude those rectangles whose boundary passes through the center point. We can count these rectangles as follows: the number of rectangles with the center of the grid lying in the interior of its south edge is $3 \times 3 \times 3=27$ (there are three choices for each of the three other edges); the number of rectangles whose south-west vertex coincides with the center is $3 \times 3=9$. Summing over all 4 orientations, we see that the total number of rectangles to exclude is $4(27+9)=144$. Therefore, the answer is $441-144=297$.
